s1.syndrome_frame: A slowly growing vascular tumor on the scalp
salient_findings: 8-mm red, firm, mobile nodule on the left temporal scalp
Irregular red lacunae with irregular vessels and absence of septa on dermoscopic evaluation
Well-circumscribed dermal vascular tumor with ectatic thin-walled vessels and intravascular branching papillary structures on histopathology
key_facts: The patient is a man in his 40s
The patient has no significant medical history
The tumor is located on the left temporal scalp
The tumor is 8-mm in size
The tumor is red, firm, and mobile
Dermoscopic evaluation showed irregular red lacunae with irregular vessels and absence of septa
Histopathology showed a well-circumscribed dermal vascular tumor
The tumor extends to the superficial subcutaneous tissue
The tumor is composed of ectatic thin-walled vessels with multiple intravascular branching papillary structures
The structures are covered by swollen endothelial cells with numerous intracytoplasmic eosinophilic hyaline globules
PAS staining showed positive hyaline globules in the cytoplasm of endothelial cells
Tumor vessels were positive for CD-31 and negative for D2-40 and HHV-8
